meaning: A calm, pleasant place in the middle of trouble or noise; also a green place with water in a desert
trick: OASIS = an O of green in the desert sand.
examples: The only oasis of silence was made by the young fellow and the old woman gazing at each other.
The small park is an oasis of calm in the busy city.

meaning: Something you must do because of a law, promise or moral duty
trick: OBLIGATION ~ OBLIGE: you are BOUND (Latin ligare, to tie) to do it.
examples: I am following the dictates of my conscience and a sacred obligation.
I feel an obligation to help my parents.

usage.pattern: have an obligation to do something / be under an obligation

meaning: Done because it is expected or required, often as a habit rather than with real feeling
trick: OBLIGATORY = an OBLIGATION you go through, like a ritual.
examples: There were the obligatory questions and the routine answers.
Wearing a helmet is obligatory on this bike ride.

meaning: Feeling that you must do something because it is expected or right; also grateful
trick: OBLIGED = tied (ligare) to it: you feel you HAVE to.
examples: People around you felt obliged to comment on your embarrassing mistake.
I felt obliged to help him after he helped me.

usage.pattern: feel obliged to do something / be obliged to someone

meaning: To destroy or remove something completely so that no trace is left
trick: OB-LITERATE: rub out every LETTER (litera) until nothing is left.
examples: They wanted to obliterate every memory of her.
Heavy rain can obliterate footprints in the sand.

meaning: Destroys or removes something completely so nothing is left
hindi: पूरी तरह मिटा देता है, नष्ट करता है
trick: OB-LITERATE-S: rubs out every LETTER of it.
examples: Facing our own death obliterates all the fragile, shallow values in life.
The new paint obliterates the old writing on the wall.

meaning: A state of empty nothingness; also the state of being completely forgotten
trick: OBLIVION ~ OBLIVIOUS: where everything is lost and forgotten.
examples: I see the edge where the rock meets oblivion.
Many old singers have faded into oblivion.

usage.pattern: fade/sink into oblivion / be lost to oblivion

meaning: Not aware of something that is happening around you
trick: OBLIVIOUS = OBLIVION in your head: you don't notice a thing.
examples: He went into the garage, oblivious to the danger moving in from behind.
She was oblivious to the noise and kept reading.

meaning: Having a long shape with four straight sides, longer than it is wide
trick: OB-LONG: a box stretched LONG.
examples: The voice came from an oblong metal plaque on the right-hand wall.
We bought an oblong table for the dining room.

usage.pattern: an oblong + noun / oblong in shape

meaning: Extremely unpleasant or annoying
trick: OB-NOXIOUS: as NOXIOUS (poisonous) as fumes.
examples: Not many people want to suffer through long commutes and obnoxious paperwork.
The obnoxious man kept shouting on the train.

meaning: So wrong or out of place that it seems offensive; also sexually indecent
trick: OB-SCENE: something that should be kept OFF the SCENE.
examples: In that rich house, even the idea of hardship seemed somehow obscene.
It is obscene to waste so much food while people starve.

usage.pattern: it is obscene to do something / an obscene + noun

meaning: Not well known, or strange and hard to understand; also to hide something from view
trick: OBSCURE = in the dark (Latin obscurus): few people see it.
examples: In 2005, most ultra races were pretty obscure.
He loves listening to obscure old bands.

meaning: A mental condition in which a person has unwanted thoughts and feels forced to repeat certain actions
trick: OCD: OBSESSIVE thoughts + COMPULSIVE actions, again and again.
examples: The BBC followed teenagers with obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) through their therapy.
Washing his hands fifty times a day was a sign of obsessive-compulsive disorder.

usage.pattern: have / suffer from / be diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder

meaning: Refusing to change your mind or behaviour, even when you should
trick: OBSTINATE: stands OBSTinately in the way like an OBSTacle.
examples: Mammy was as obstinate and uncompromising as the Mujahideen.
My obstinate little brother refused to eat his vegetables.

usage.pattern: be obstinate (about something) / an obstinate + noun

meaning: The huge areas of salt water that cover most of the earth
trick: OCEANS: O-SEA-NS, the biggest seas.
examples: I bounced back and forth across countries and oceans for over five years.
Plastic waste is harming our oceans.

meaning: A dull yellowish-brown or orange-brown colour; also an earth used to make this colour
trick: OCHRE sounds like OKRA: a yellow-brown earth colour.
examples: Around them, the trees had started to turn ochre and orange, scarlet red.
The old house was painted a warm ochre.

meaning: Something made to praise and honour someone or something, especially a poem
trick: ODE: an O-DEar poem to someone you love.
examples: Queen Gauhar Shad raised the minarets as her loving ode to Herat.
He wrote a short ode to his mother's cooking.

meaning: Very unpleasant and causing strong dislike
trick: ODIOUS ~ ODIUM/HATE: something you HATE (Latin odium).
examples: I realised how odious I would find this.
Cheating the poor is an odious act.

usage.pattern: be odious (to someone) / an odious + noun

meaning: Not ready for something that happens suddenly
trick: OFF GUARD: the GUARD is OFF duty, so anything can get in.
examples: A flare of pride caught her off guard.
The sudden question caught me off guard.

meaning: Said privately and not meant to be reported or made public
trick: OFF the RECORD: the recorder is switched OFF.
examples: He also shared some off the record wisdom.
The minister spoke to the reporter off the record.

usage.pattern: speak off the record / an off-the-record + noun

meaning: The part of the sea far away but still visible from the shore; also (used after in the) likely to happen soon
trick: OFFING = the sea far OFF from the shore.
examples: We rushed along the waterfront, with masts swaying in the offing.
A storm was gathering in the offing; a promotion is in the offing too.

meaning: Cotton cloth covered with oil or plastic so that water cannot pass through
trick: OIL + CLOTH: cloth soaked in OIL so rain runs off.
examples: She carried an oilcloth bag with our bathing kit and a towel.
Grandma covered the kitchen table with oilcloth.

usage.pattern: an oilcloth + bag/cover / covered with oilcloth

meaning: A green vegetable pod with seeds inside, cooked as a vegetable
trick: OKRA = OK, RAh! bhindi for lunch.
examples: Mariam put the rice and the lamb and okra qurma in front of him.
My mother makes tasty fried okra.

meaning: A sign that something good or bad will happen in the future
trick: OMEN: an O! MEN look up when they see a sign.
examples: Is it a bad omen to tie shoes together and hang them from a nail?
Some people think a black cat is a bad omen.

meaning: Something that has been left out or not done
trick: OMISSION ~ OMIT: the thing you OMITted.
examples: He made no reference to the funeral, and this seemed a serious omission.
Her name was missing from the list, a careless omission.

meaning: Things that have been left out by mistake
trick: OMISSIONS ~ OMIT: all the things you OMITted.
examples: Any omissions brought to our attention will be fixed in future editions.
The report had a few omissions that we corrected.

usage.pattern: omissions from something / errors and omissions

meaning: With hands and knees on the ground
trick: ALL FOUR limbs touching the ground, like a dog.
examples: One moment she was talking and the next she was on all fours.
The baby crawled on all fours.

usage.pattern: be / get down on all fours

meaning: On the side that is farther away from you
hindi: के उस पार, की दूसरी ओर
trick: FAR SIDE = the side FAR from you.
examples: He sat down facing me, on the far side of Mother.
The shop is on the far side of the road.

usage.pattern: on the far side of something/someone
partners: on the far side of the room
on the far side of the river

meaning: Considering everything; in general
trick: ON THE WHOLE: look at the WHOLE picture, not the parts.
examples: On the whole, however, they seemed tired and exhausted.
On the whole, the trip was a lot of fun.

partners: on the whole, it was good

meaning: A person who watches something happen but does not take part
trick: ON-LOOKER: someone who just LOOKS ON.
examples: I pictured being an onlooker who comes to see the show and then goes home.
A crowd of onlookers gathered after the accident.

meaning: The beginning of something, especially something bad
trick: ON-SET: the moment it is SET ON.
examples: The baby's sounds signalled the onset of a hearty cry.
Close the windows before the onset of winter.

meaning: A strong, violent attack; also a large amount of something that is hard to deal with
trick: ON-SLAUGHT: rushing ON to SLAUGHTER.
examples: It is a story of romance, intrigue and the onslaught of war.
The small shop could not survive the onslaught of online sales.

usage.pattern: the onslaught of something / an onslaught on/against something

meaning: Flowed out slowly in small amounts
trick: OOZED: slow as OOZE (mud) pushing out.
examples: Sweat oozed from my pores, but after a short rest I took more pain.
Honey oozed out of the cracked jar.

meaning: Flowing out slowly in small amounts; also showing a lot of a quality
trick: OOZING: slow like OOZE (mud) creeping out.
examples: Honey was oozing slowly out of the broken jar.
The cake was oozing with chocolate.

usage.pattern: be oozing (with) something / oozing from something

meaning: Difficult to understand or explain; also not letting light through
trick: OPAQUE: no light passes, like an OPAQUE glass: you can't see through it.
examples: These questions feel impossibly complex and opaque.
The rules of the new tax system are opaque to most people.

meaning: A play in which the words are sung to music
trick: OPERA: a big drama where everyone sings, OPEn-mouthed.
examples: Hell Week is the devil's opera, and it builds like a crescendo.
We went to see an opera in Italy.

usage.pattern: go to the opera / an opera singer

meaning: A strong drug made from the juice of poppy seeds
trick: OPIUM ~ OPIATE: the sleepy drug from the POPPY.
examples: Orwell was born in the middle of a highly productive opium district.
Opium is made from poppy plants.

meaning: Completely different from something else; also on the other side, facing
trick: OPPOSITE: OPPOSing side.
examples: But she chose the opposite.
Hot is the opposite of cold.

usage.pattern: the opposite (of something) / do the opposite

meaning: Cruel and unfair treatment of people, especially by those in power
trick: OPPRESSION: PRESSing people down.
examples: It brings home the indignities of war and oppression.
The people fought against years of oppression.

meaning: Great wealth and costly, rich comfort
trick: OPULENCE ~ OPULENT: lots of OPtions and plENty of money.
examples: Despite the endless luxury and opulence, the prince became an angry young man.
The hotel was full of gold and opulence.

usage.pattern: the opulence of something / live in opulence

meaning: A piece of land where fruit trees are grown
trick: ORCHARD: ORCH(ard) = a yARD of fruit trees.
examples: They spent their Sundays together in the small paddock beyond the orchard.
We picked apples in my uncle's orchard.

usage.pattern: in/beyond the orchard / an apple orchard

meaning: Carefully planned and organised, often secretly
trick: ORCHESTRATED: arranged like an ORCHESTRA, every part in its place.
examples: At night, this careful, mutually orchestrated dance of avoidance was not possible.
The surprise party was orchestrated by her friends.

usage.pattern: something is orchestrated by someone / a carefully orchestrated + noun

meaning: A very difficult, painful or upsetting experience
trick: ORDEAL: an ORDEr to DEAL with pain.
examples: This ordeal must be very hard for you.
Waiting for the test results was an ordeal.

meaning: A part of the body that does a special job, such as the heart or a wing; also a large musical instrument
trick: ORGAN: the body's ORGANised working parts.
examples: A bird's wing is an organ of movement, not of handling things.
The heart is the organ that pumps blood.

usage.pattern: an organ of something / organ + donor/transplant

meaning: Wild parties with too much drinking, drugs or sex; also a lot of some activity
trick: ORGIES: ORGanised wild parties.
examples: Choosing a good marriage means not making wild orgies a big part of my life.
The ancient kings were famous for their drunken orgies.

meaning: To set or direct something, such as your mind, in a particular way; also to find your position
trick: ORIENT = the East, where the sun rises: you turn to face the right direction.
examples: You simply have to orient your mind in a certain way to experience it.
It takes a few days to orient yourself in a new city.

usage.pattern: orient something towards something / orient yourself

meaning: An opening in the body, such as the mouth, nose or ear; also any small hole
trick: ORIFICE sounds like 'OR-I-FACE': the openings in your face.
examples: They wanted sand in our ears, up our noses, and in every orifice of our body.
The doctor checked every orifice for signs of infection.

usage.pattern: an orifice of something / every orifice

meaning: Openings in the body, such as the mouth, nose or ears; also small holes
trick: ORIFICES = more than one ORIFICE: ears, nose, mouth.
examples: Sand got into the ears, nose and other orifices of the swimmers.
Germs can enter the body through its natural orifices.

usage.pattern: the orifices of something / through orifices

meaning: A bright yellow or orange songbird
trick: ORIOLE sounds like 'AUREOLE' (golden): a golden bird.
examples: Outside, an oriole was warbling.
A yellow oriole sat singing on the mango tree.

meaning: An object used to decorate a place, such as a garden or room
trick: ORNAMENT looks like 'ADORNMENT': things that adorn.
examples: Don't worry about buying that new lawn ornament.
She hung a shiny ornament on the Christmas tree.

usage.pattern: a + noun + ornament / an ornament on something

meaning: A home where children without parents are looked after
trick: ORPHAN + AGE: the place where ORPHANs live and grow up.
examples: The orphanage director was a stooping, narrow-chested man with a kind face.
The children at the orphanage got new books today.

usage.pattern: live in an orphanage / the orphanage director

meaning: Children whose parents have died
trick: ORPHANS sound like 'OFF-PARENTS': children whose parents are gone.
examples: Zaman seemed gently protective of the orphans.
The charity gives food and school books to orphans.

usage.pattern: look after orphans / orphans of the war

meaning: A very small amount of something, such as courage or strength; also a unit of weight (about 28 grams)
trick: Every OUNCE = every little bit, down to the last ounce.
examples: It would take every ounce of courage I had to pull off the impossible.
She doesn't have an ounce of fear in her.

usage.pattern: every ounce of something / not an ounce of something

meaning: Breathing quickly and with difficulty, usually after running or effort
trick: Your BREATH has run OUT: you're gasping for more.
examples: We were both out of breath, and the bumpy truck ride made it worse.
I was out of breath after climbing the stairs.

meaning: Informal: not working or arranged properly; out of balance
trick: One WHACK on the machine and now it's OUT OF WHACK.
examples: If our values are poorly chosen, everything based on them will be out of whack.
My sleep has been out of whack since the trip.

usage.pattern: be out of whack / knock something out of whack

meaning: A person who has been rejected or pushed out by society or a group
trick: Cast OUT of the group = OUTCAST.
examples: He was willing to be different, an outcast, a pariah, for the sake of his values.
The new boy felt like an outcast at school.

usage.pattern: be/feel like an outcast / a social outcast

meaning: A loud shout or noise of alarm; also a strong public protest
trick: OUT + CRY: everyone cries OUT loud together.
examples: When the hens heard this, they raised a terrible outcry.
There was a public outcry when the park was closed.

usage.pattern: raise an outcry / an outcry over/against something

meaning: Grew too big for something, such as clothes or an artificial leg; also left behind a habit as you grew up
hindi: बड़ा हो गया (उसके लिए छोटा पड़ा)
trick: Grew OUT of it: OUTGREW the old shoes.
examples: Tariq outgrew his leg again and was given a new one by the Red Cross.
My son outgrew his school shoes in just three months.

meaning: A small toilet building outside a house; also a small shed near a house
trick: A HOUSE OUTside the house = OUTHOUSE.
examples: She pushed on doors until one opened, and she saw the outhouse, the well, the toolshed.
The old farm had an outhouse behind the kitchen.

usage.pattern: go to the outhouse / an outhouse behind something

meaning: Small buildings or sheds near a main house, used for storage; also outdoor toilets
trick: OUT-HOUSES: little houses OUTside the big one.
examples: Plenty of sand and cement had been found in one of the outhouses.
The farmer kept his tools in the outhouses.

usage.pattern: in one of the outhouses / the outhouses of a farm

meaning: To keep going longer than someone or something
trick: OUT + LAST: you LAST and they drop OUT.
examples: That realization gave me the edge I needed to outlast Psycho Pete one more time.
Good shoes will outlast cheap ones by years.

meaning: Kept going longer than someone or something
trick: OUTLASTED = he quit first, you LASTED.
examples: That's when I knew I'd outlasted him.
The old car outlasted all our newer ones.

meaning: A person or thing very different from the rest of a group
trick: OUT-LIER: it LIEs OUTside the group, far from the others.
examples: He thought I was a medical marvel, some kind of outlier.
Her test score was an outlier; everyone else scored much lower.

usage.pattern: be an outlier / an outlier in something

meaning: Living or lasting longer than someone or something
trick: OUT-LIVING: still LIVING after the other is gone.
examples: When our self outliving our body no longer seems possible, fear of death creeps back.
She is outliving all her old friends.

meaning: A person's general attitude or way of seeing things; also what is likely to happen in the future
trick: How you LOOK OUT at the world = your OUTLOOK.
examples: Major's speech gave the animals a completely new outlook on life.
She has a positive outlook even on bad days.

usage.pattern: an outlook on something / the outlook for something

meaning: Strong anger and shock at something unfair or wrong; also an act that causes it
trick: OUT + RAGE: RAGE spilling OUT.
examples: I appreciated his outrage.
There was outrage when the prices doubled overnight.

meaning: Completely and immediately; also openly and directly
trick: OUT + RIGHT: RIGHT OUT, all at once, nothing left.
examples: Do you really think that when you die you die outright, and nothing remains?
He refused outright to help us.

usage.pattern: do something outright / refuse/reject something outright

meaning: The outer parts of a town or city, far from the centre
trick: The SKIRT is the outer edge of a dress: OUTSKIRTS = outer edge of a city.
examples: On the outskirts of the thousand-year-old city lived a philosopher.
They bought a house on the outskirts of Pune.

meaning: The habit of saying exactly what you think, even if it upsets people
trick: Words SPOKEN OUT loud without a filter = OUTSPOKENNESS.
examples: In the West such outspokenness is seen as offensive, especially from someone you just met.
Her outspokenness made her popular with some and disliked by others.

meaning: To be more important or greater than something else
hindi: से भारी पड़ना, से ज़्यादा होना
trick: On a scale, one side WEIGHs more and wins OUT.
examples: It would have taken a lot of failures to outweigh the advantage.
The benefits of exercise outweigh the effort.

meaning: Looking or speaking backwards past your shoulder, towards someone behind you
hindi: पीछे मुड़कर, कंधे के ऊपर से
trick: Your voice or eyes go OVER YOUR SHOULDER to the person behind.
examples: He raised his voice and called over his shoulder, "We're going now, Fariba!"
She looked over her shoulder to see who was following.

meaning: Covered with grey clouds, so the sun cannot be seen
trick: Clouds CAST OVER the sky = OVERCAST.
examples: One cold, overcast day in January, they went to watch the Soviet convoys leave.
It was overcast all morning, so we took umbrellas.

meaning: To try too hard to make up for a weakness or problem
trick: OVER + COMPENSATE: making up for it, but OVER the limit.
examples: I felt a constant need to overcompensate, to prove that I was loved.
Shy people sometimes overcompensate by talking too loudly.

usage.pattern: overcompensate for something / overcompensate by doing something

meaning: Heard what other people were saying without them knowing or meaning you to
hindi: चुपके से सुना, अनजाने में सुना
trick: The words came OVER the wall and you HEARD them.
examples: Mariam resented them when she overheard them complaining about their sons.
I overheard my neighbours talking about the new shop.

usage.pattern: overheard someone doing something / overheard something

meaning: Not noticed or not given the attention deserved; also had a view over a place
trick: Your eyes LOOKED OVER it and missed it.
examples: In life, there is no gift as overlooked as failure.
Her hard work was overlooked by the manager.

meaning: Having a view of a place from above
trick: LOOKING OVER the street from a high seat.
examples: I slid into a seat above the back tire, overlooking the street.
We stayed in a hotel overlooking the lake.

meaning: Has a view of a place from above; also fails to notice something
hindi: की ओर खुलता है, सामने है; नज़रअंदाज़ करता है
trick: The building LOOKS OVER the sea.
examples: Our building overlooks the sea.
My bedroom window overlooks the park.

meaning: Watched over and managed a job or activity
trick: He SAW OVER everything: OVERSAW = supervised.
examples: Ahmad Shah Massoud personally oversaw the burial.
My father oversaw the building of our new house.

meaning: Made someone or something seem less important or noticed; also made sad or gloomy
trick: Their big SHADOW fell OVER her, so no one saw her.
examples: They had overshadowed her in life.
His sister's success overshadowed his own.

usage.pattern: overshadowed someone/something / be overshadowed by something

meaning: To push yourself too hard so that you get hurt or exhausted
hindi: ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा ज़ोर लगाना, थका देना
trick: STRAIN OVER the limit = OVERSTRAIN.
examples: Clover warned him to be careful not to overstrain himself.
Don't overstrain your back lifting those boxes.

meaning: Made to do or cover too much, so that it cannot work well
hindi: हद से ज़्यादा फैला हुआ, बोझ से दबा
trick: Like a rubber band STRETCHED OVER its limit, ready to snap.
examples: Their economy was floundering and their military overstretched across half of Asia.
The hospital staff are overstretched this winter.

meaning: Done or shown openly, not hidden
trick: OVERT is the opposite of cOVERT: nothing is cOVERed.
examples: Your life is not ruined because of overt racists or hidden unfairness.
There was overt anger in his voice.

meaning: The act of removing a ruler or government from power by force
trick: THROW the ruler OVER and OUT of the throne.
examples: Work night and day, body and soul, for the overthrow of the human race!
The rebels planned the overthrow of the king.

meaning: Removed from power by force
hindi: सत्ता से हटाया गया, तख़्ता पलटा गया
trick: The king was THROWN OVER = OVERTHROWN.
examples: King Zahir Shah had been overthrown in a bloodless coup.
The dictator was overthrown by his own army.

usage.pattern: be overthrown by someone / be overthrown in something

meaning: Suddenly affected someone strongly, as a feeling; also went past a slower vehicle or person
hindi: घेर लिया, हावी हो गया; आगे निकल गया
trick: Sadness came OVER him and TOOK him: OVERTOOK.
examples: Bouts of depression overtook him for weeks at a time.
Fear overtook her when the lights went out.

meaning: Friendly attempts to start a relationship or make peace with someone
trick: Like an OVERTURE that opens a song, these open a friendship.
examples: But these overtures are dismissed by Zalmai, sometimes angrily.
She ignored all his friendly overtures.

usage.pattern: make overtures to someone / reject someone's overtures

meaning: Having a right to receive something from someone; also needed to pay back money
trick: OWED = 'O, it's due!': something you have a right to get.
examples: I knew I wasn't owed an explanation.
She owed her friend a hundred rupees.

usage.pattern: be owed something / owed someone something

meaning: Large male cattle used for pulling carts or ploughs (plural of ox)
trick: One OX, two OXEN, like one child, two children.
examples: The old computer game had sickness and drowning oxen and everything.
The farmer used two oxen to plough his field.

usage.pattern: a pair of oxen / oxen pull something
